text:
Jim stood at the back of the studio, sweating profusely, trying to mimic the serene grace of the woman in front of him. He was attempting a complex variation of the "Tree Pose," but his balance was less "bamboo" and more "wobbly jelly." As he lifted his leg, his foot slipped, sending him into a desperate flail. To stabilize himself, he let out a sharp, involuntary grunt that echoed off the mirrored walls.

The instructor, a woman named Serenity who took her zen very seriously, paused mid-flow. "Jim," she said softly, her voice trembling with suppressed laughter, "perhaps we should start with the 'Child's Pose'?"

Jim, red-faced and tangled in his own limbs, tried to apologize but ended up twisting his torso so sharply that a loud, resonant *toot* escaped him. The entire class froze. For a second, there was silence. Then, the woman in front of him snorted. Then another student giggled. Within moments, the sacred silence of the advanced class was shattered by a chorus of suppressed chuckles.

Just as Jim was about to crawl out of the room in shame, the door burst open. A tall, lanky man walked in, looking confused. It was Gary, Jim’s cousin, who had been sent to pick up his dry cleaning. Gary, unaware of the yoga context, looked around at the room full of people in various states of undignified contortion. He spotted Jim, who was currently trying to hide behind a yoga mat.

"Jim!" Gary called out, his voice booming. "I found your shirt! It’s in the bag."

Jim froze, still holding a pose that looked suspiciously like a question mark. Gary, oblivious to the tension, walked further into the room, his long legs carrying him past the rows of yogis. As he leaned down to hand the bag to Jim, his neck stretched out like a crane’s, creating an absurd visual contrast with the hunched, grunting yogis.

"Sorry I'm late," Gary said, his long neck bobbing as he smiled. "Traffic was a nightmare. I had to take the scenic route."

The class erupted. Not just in laughter, but in genuine, tears-streaming-down-their-faces hilarity. The image of Gary’s elongated neck juxtaposed against Jim’s failed yoga attempts was too much. Even Serenity couldn't hold it together; she collapsed onto her mat
